gather.answer: Draft answer for 5.1.2, from the evidence found.

requirements.reason: The register lists every transfer service with its use and protection.

citations.quote: On 8 September 2026 IT tested each service from outside our network with a TLS scanning tool: no service accepted a connection without encryption, and none offered a protocol older than TLS 1.2.
IT keeps a register of the network services we use to send information in and out of the company, such as email, the supplier portal and the customer exchange platform.

requirements.reason: Rules per classification are defined, and the register sets each service's highest classification.

citations.quote: On 8 September 2026 IT tested each service from outside our network with a TLS scanning tool: no service accepted a connection without encryption, and none offered a protocol older than TLS 1.2.

We may also use services run by outside providers, once IT and the information security officer have approved them; the approved ones are listed in the cloud services register, each with its owner, the highest classification it may hold, where the data is kept and the contract.

requirements.reason: Encryption in transit on every service, confirmed by the September scan.

citations.quote: On 8 September 2026 IT tested each service from outside our network with a TLS scanning tool: no service accepted a connection without encryption, and none offered a protocol older than TLS 1.2.
The customer exchange platform encrypts files both in transit and at rest, and logs every download.

requirements.reason: Nothing covers sending information to the right recipient.
Confidential data goes only by the platform or end-to-end encrypted email.

citations.quote: Customer exchange platform | Drawings and prototype data | Strictly confidential | TLS 1.3; files encrypted at rest; downloads logged | 2026-09-08
Confidential information, including all customer drawings and prototype data, may be sent only through the customer exchange platform or by email encrypted end to end.
